## Questions

Is AppuBot free? Yes, during early access, with no account and no card. You only keep paying for the AI plan you already have, like Claude or ChatGPT.

Is AppuBot a Grok Bot alternative? Yes. Like Grok Bot, it gives you a team of named AI bots you message like colleagues. Unlike it, they run on your own computer, use the apps on it, and can use Claude, ChatGPT (Codex), Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode or Grok.

Does AppuBot run on Windows and Linux? Yes. It's made for the Mac first, with Windows and Linux versions too, computer use included.

Where does my data go? It stays on your computer. What leaves is what a bot sends to its AI provider, such as Anthropic or OpenAI, just like when you use that AI yourself. [...] | AppuBot | Grok Bot | OpenAI dots | Meta Muse |
 ---  --- |
| Price | Free during early access | $30 to $200 a month, plus extra usage | ChatGPT Pro, $100 to $500 a month, or Business Premium | Free up to a limit, then $20 or $100 a month |
| Uses the apps on your computer | Yes, any app, in its own window | No, it works on its own cloud computer | Partly: a connected computer gives it your files and browser | No, it works in a cloud browser |
| AI model | Your choice: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Grok or OpenCode | Grok only | GPT-6 Astra only | Muse Spark only |
| How many agents | As many bots as you like | Many bots, sharing one cloud computer | One dot to start | One Muse per person | [...] From the makers' own pages, as of 17 October 2026. Sources and the full comparison: appubot.com/compare.

## An alternative to MausBot, OpenBot, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Manus and Claude Cowork

Looking at MausBot, OpenBot, OpenClaw or Hermes Agent for AI bots on your own computer, or at Manus or Claude Cowork for an agent that does the work for you? AppuBot is one app you install and use straight away:

 Nothing to host or set up: no server, no Docker, no API keys.
 Its bots use any app on your Mac or PC, clicking and typing in its own window, while you watch their cursor.
 It runs the AI you already pay for, a different one per bot if you like.
 Each bot can answer you on Telegram, from anywhere.

results.content:
Setup was easy for me with one exception: configuring the CLIs. I had Claude Desktop walk me through that part, and it worked. It's Mac-only today, with Windows next and Linux and Ubuntu after that.

## The Rough Edges, Because It Launched a Day Ago

This is open source and it literally just launched, so expect some mess.

 Formatting glitches in places. It's launch-day software.
 It only runs on Claude, Codex and Grok for now.
 The approvals get repetitive.
 Agent-to-agent tagging didn't work when I tested it. Grok Bot has that working, and I'd expect a fix, but today it's broken.
 It's not a polished big-company product, and it doesn't pretend to be.

## When You'd Still Pick Grok Bot [...] ## When You'd Still Pick Grok Bot

If you want the smoothest, most polished version of this idea and you don't mind paying, Grok Bot is that product — once you clear the waitlist and accept the meter. For everyone else, the Grok Bot free alternative gets you most of the idea for none of the money.

| Feature | Grok Bot | OpenMausBot |
 --- 
| Price | Paid and metered, behind a waitlist | Free, runs on subscriptions you already have |
| Access | Early beta invite | GitHub download today |
| Models | Fixed, no switching | Per bot: Fable 5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Haiku, Codex, Grok 4.5 |
| Agent-to-agent tagging | Works | Broken in my test, for now |
| Polish | Big-company smooth | Day-one open source |

## Grok Bot Free Alternative FAQ

### Is OpenMausBot really free? [...] Locked out of Grok Bot's waitlist? You're in good company — and a proper Grok Bot free alternative dropped just one day after the beta went live. It's called OpenMausBot (you'll also see it written Open MouseBot), it's open source, and instead of asking for another subscription it runs on the AI tools you're already logged into. I got hands on with it the day it dropped, ran it side by side with Grok Bot, and for most people I think it's the smarter place to start.
